body:
OWNER RESPONSE — sequencing correction accepted. `instrument-core` is a conditional extraction boundary, not the next implementation artifact. The three typed spikes must discover its real common mechanics first; otherwise we would generalize the current Discourse Atlas tracer and call that architecture.

Two refinements to my post:

1. I retract `RepresentationTier` as a proposed new ADT for now. It was meant to name screen-space representation pressure, but the existing mapping must be made explicit first: `NarrativeLevel` says what narrative object is represented, `SurfaceDetail` says how much source detail is shown, and `FeatureScale` says what a measurement means. The instrument map should show all three independently and expose the current hardcoded `SurfaceDetail.Hidden` / absent feature choice. Only after the spikes should we decide whether screen-space budgeting needs a new type or is a policy over the existing contracts.

2. The renderer capability matrix begins as an inventory with honest unknowns, not a mandate to build a kernel. Static SVG, Canvas, names, viewports, clipping, and determinism are demonstrated. Retained update, camera, picking, culling, collision, and large-mark performance remain `unmeasured` until the typed spikes exercise them. ADR D7 remains the gate.

I agree with the provider consequences: Chronology Loom starts with a new `ProjectionKind` and `ProjectionContract` in storymodel4s, never a restyled DiscourseAtlas; the first feature visualization distinguishes the four existing channel states before it paints any value, then consumes checked sidecar materialization and declared WindowPlans; Recall starts from AlignmentMatrix with Source / Distorted / External distinct and dual-Codex ribbons remain blocked on the joined trace. The visual grammar should indeed begin with existing enums and derived quantities. If no type owns a proposed mark, it is a design question, not a renderer task.

My architectural claim narrows to this: once those spikes reveal genuinely repeated camera, picking, correspondence, or layer-budget mechanics, keep them in a story-agnostic module with Intaglio behind an adapter so they are liftable. Do not pre-build that module. This preserves the users requested extraction boundary without pretending we already know its abstraction.
